name: auto-import
description: Generate ready-made relative-path imports with one keystroke. Pick a file in the Explorer; the right import — JS, TS, JSX, TSX, CSS, SCSS, HTML, or Markdown — lands in your editor. Angular-aware naming, SCSS partial support, and 20+ configurable styles.

commands.title: Auto Import: Insert Import from Selected File
Auto Import: Paste as Import (Pick Style)
Auto Import: Set Default Import Style

auto-import.preferences.importStatementP.title: Import statement placement
auto-import.preferences.importStatementP.description: Where to insert generated import statements in the destination file. Forced to 'Cursor' for HTML, Markdown, and when importing a non-stylesheet into a stylesheet — those contexts only make sense at the cursor and the user setting is ignored. Default: Bottom.
enumDescriptions: Insert before the first line of the file.
Append after the last recognised import / require / @import / @use line. Falls back to line 0 if no import is found.
Insert at the current cursor position.

auto-import.importStatement.script.prese.title: Preserve script file extension in imports
auto-import.importStatement.script.prese.description: Keep the source .js / .ts / .jsx / .tsx extension on the generated import path. Most module systems (Node, bundlers, TypeScript) omit it by convention, which is why this is off by default.

auto-import.importStatement.script.javas.title: JavaScript / JSX import style
auto-import.importStatement.script.javas.description: Template used for .js destinations, and for .js / .jsx sources imported into .jsx or .tsx files. '_relativePath_' is replaced with the computed relative path; 'name' becomes a snippet placeholder so your cursor lands on it after insertion.
enumDescriptions: ES module: namespace import (every export bound under one name)

auto-import.importStatement.script.types.title: TypeScript / TSX import style
auto-import.importStatement.script.types.description: Template used for .ts destinations, and for .ts / .tsx sources imported into .tsx files. '_relativePath_' is replaced with the computed relative path; 'name' becomes a snippet placeholder. With the 'import { name }' shape, Angular file conventions (.component, .directive, .pipe, .service, .module) auto-fill 'name' with a PascalCase identifier derived from the basename — for example, app-root.component.ts becomes { AppRootComponent }.
enumDescriptions: ES module: named import — Angular files (.component / .directive / .pipe / .service / .module) auto-fill PascalCase identifiers
ES module: namespace import (every export bound under one name)

auto-import.importStatement.styleSheet.p.title: Preserve stylesheet file extension in imports
auto-import.importStatement.styleSheet.p.description: Keep the source .css / .scss extension on the generated import path. Exception: .css extensions are always preserved inside .scss imports — Sass requires the extension to recognise a foreign-language import, and this setting has no effect there.

auto-import.importStatement.styleSheet.c.title: CSS @import style
auto-import.importStatement.styleSheet.c.description: Template used when a .css source is imported into a .css destination. '_relativePath_' is replaced with the computed relative path.

auto-import.importStatement.styleSheet.c.title: CSS image reference style
auto-import.importStatement.styleSheet.c.description: Snippet used when an image source is imported into a .css destination — typically for background-image, content, mask-image, and similar properties. '_relativePath_' is replaced with the computed relative path.

auto-import.importStatement.styleSheet.s.title: SCSS @import / @use style
auto-import.importStatement.styleSheet.s.description: Template used when a .scss or .css source is imported into a .scss destination. Modern Sass uses @use for a true module system; legacy Sass uses @import. Leading underscores on partial filenames (e.g. _variables.scss) are stripped automatically to match Sass's partial-resolution convention.
enumDescriptions: Modern @use with wildcard alias — no namespace prefix required

auto-import.importStatement.styleSheet.s.title: SCSS image reference style
auto-import.importStatement.styleSheet.s.description: Snippet used when an image source is imported into a .scss destination. Reuses the CSS image template — the url() syntax is identical between the two languages.

auto-import.importStatement.markup.htmlS.title: HTML <script> tag style
auto-import.importStatement.markup.htmlS.description: Tag inserted at the cursor when a .js source is imported into a .html destination. '_relativePath_' is replaced with the computed relative path.

auto-import.importStatement.markup.htmlI.title: HTML tag style
auto-import.importStatement.markup.htmlI.description: Tag inserted at the cursor when an image source is imported into a .html destination. '_relativePath_' is replaced with the computed relative path.
enumDescriptions: Standard tag with placeholder alt text

auto-import.importStatement.markup.htmlS.title: HTML <link> stylesheet style
auto-import.importStatement.markup.htmlS.description: Tag inserted at the cursor when a .css source is imported into a .html destination. '_relativePath_' is replaced with the computed relative path.

auto-import.importStatement.markup.markd.title: Markdown link style
auto-import.importStatement.markup.markd.description: Snippet inserted at the cursor when a .md source is imported into a .md destination. '_relativePath_' is replaced with the computed relative path; 'text' becomes a snippet placeholder for the link's display text.

auto-import.importStatement.markup.markd.title: Markdown image style
auto-import.importStatement.markup.markd.description: Snippet inserted at the cursor when an image source is imported into a .md destination. Choose between inline syntax — ![alt](path "title") — or reference-style — ![alt][ref] / [ref]: path "title". '_relativePath_' is replaced with the computed relative path.
enumDescriptions: Inline image syntax with hover-text title
Reference-style — define [ref] once, reuse it elsewhere in the document

scripts.package: npm run check-types && npm run lint && node esbuild.js --production
